tool.name: ReadMetadata
tool.summary: Extracts and displays comprehensive metadata from GeoTIFF files with detailed HTML or Markdown reports.

usage.bullet_item: Generates detailed analysis of TIFF tags, GeoTIFF keys, projection information, and COG validation.
HTML format provides syntax highlighting and is best for viewing in web browsers.
Markdown format is plain text and useful for side-by-side comparisons for quality assurance.
Choose between Analyst (compact), Producer (complete), or Custom section selection presets.

P.SPAN: The GeoTIFF file or raster layer to analyze. You can select a layer from the map or browse to a file on disk.
Choose the output format for the metadata report. HTML provides syntax highlighting and is best for viewing, while Markdown is plain text suitable for documentation and version control.
A suffix to append to the output filename before the file extension. Default is '_meta' for metadata reports.
The generated metadata report file. This path is automatically determined based on the input file, format, and suffix selections.
When checked, the generated report file will be automatically opened using the system's default application (e.g., a web browser for HTML files).

If checked, an Esri-compatible Persistent Auxiliary Metadata (PAM) .aux.xml file containing band statistics and histograms will be created. This allows ArcGIS Pro to skip the 'Calculate Statistics' step when loading the raster. PAM is a standard format used by GDAL and ArcGIS to store raster statistics and histograms and is read by other GIS software.

The Image File Directory (IFD) number to read. Defaults to 0 (the main image). Overviews and other supplemental images are stored in subsequent IFDs. For example, a GeoTIFF with three overviews and no transparency mask will have IFDs 0-4, where IFD 0 is the main image and IFDs 1-4 are the overviews. If present, the internal transparency mask of the main image is IFD 1.
Custom text to display at the top and bottom of the report. Useful for classification markings (e.g., UNCLASSIFIED, Public Domain), source citations or project identifiers.

Predefined configuration for report content. 'Analyst' focuses on actionable data with compact tables and standard tags. 'Producer' focuses on production details with complete tag scope and raw text formats. 'Custom' allows manual selection of specific report sections.

Controls the verbosity of the TIFF Tag section. 'Compact' shows only the most useful tags. 'Complete' lists every single TIFF tag found in the header, including structural metadata (e.g. StripOffsets, TileByteCounts) or content better reported in other sections (e.g. GeoKeyDirectoryTag, ModelTiePointTag). This is redundant but allows data producers to confirm that the header is correctly formatted.

How XML metadata (GDAL_METADATA, GEO_METADATA, PAM, XMP, and external XML files) is presented in the report. 'Table' formats XML attributes into readable key-value pairs, one per row. 'Text' displays the raw XML string with syntax highlighting, useful for copy-pasting or debugging.
Detailed listing of all TIFF tags in the header, including tag IDs, names, data types, counts, and values. Essential for understanding file structure and identifying non-standard tags.
GDAL domain metadata stored in TIFF Tag 42112, including statistics per band, color interpretation, software information, and custom metadata items. Critical for understanding raster interpretation.
Adobe XMP metadata stored in TIFF Tag 700, commonly used for image provenance, copyright, and descriptive metadata in imagery workflows. Less commonly used than GDAL metadata for geospatial data.

GeoTIFF keys (largely EPSG Registry codes) that define the coordinate reference system, including projection, datum, ellipsoid, and units. The codes and their meanings are defined in the OGC GeoTIFF specification. The same information is captured in the analyst-friendly 'Spatial Reference' section.
Human-readable summary of the coordinate reference system derived from GeoKeys, including projection name, datum, ellipsoid, and units.
Six-parameter affine transformation matrix that maps pixel coordinates to geographic coordinates. Shows pixel size, origin, and skew (rotation) parameters.

Minimum and maximum X/Y coordinates of the raster extent in the native coordinate system, plus center point coordinates. The extents are calculated from the GeoTransform parameters. The raster type (PixelIsArea or PixelIsPoint) is also considered in defining the extent. A PixelIsArea raster extends 1/2 pixel outside the edge pixel centers, while a PixelIsPoint raster extent fall on the outer extents of the raster. In contrast, GDAL does NOT take raster type into account when calculating the bounding box, treating every raster based on an area interpretation of pixels.
Geographic extent in latitude/longitude (WGS84), including corner coordinates and center point. Useful for quick geographic location identification.
Band statistics including minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation, and NoData handling. Shows data value ranges and quality.
Visual histogram chart showing the distribution of pixel values for each band. Helps identify data ranges, outliers, and quality issues.
Esri Projection Engine string stored in GDAL metadata, used by ArcGIS software for CRS identification. May differ from standard WKT representation.
Well Known Text version 2 (WKT2) representation of the coordinate reference system, following OGC GeoTIFF v1.1 standard. The authoritative CRS definition.
JSON representation of the coordinate reference system following PROJ conventions. Modern alternative to WKT for CRS exchange.
Internal tiling configuration and overview pyramid structure. Shows tile dimensions, overview levels, and resampling methods. Critical for performance analysis.
Complete list of all Image File Directories (IFDs) in the file, including main image, transparency mask, and overview pages. Shows dimensions, compression, and structure.
Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) validation results showing compliance with COG specification. Identifies issues that prevent efficient HTTP range request access.
Embedded XML metadata stored in TIFF Tag 50909, often containing ISO 19115/19139 metadata or custom XML from external sidecar files.
Content from external XML sidecar file (e.g., .tif.xml), typically ISO metadata or custom XML documentation accompanying the GeoTIFF.
GDAL Persistent Auxiliary Metadata from .aux.xml file, including statistics, histograms, color tables, and rat band interpretation used by ArcGIS and other GDAL-based software.
